rationale: The plan correctly identifies that n=1 per condition makes within-group dispersion unestimable, refuses to report inferential p-values, delivers size-factor-normalized counts with shrunken descriptive log2FC, and adds a power/sample-size step that names the replication needed for a valid follow-up — all matching the reference. It loses points for nonetheless running DESeq2/edgeR under assumed fixed dispersions and reporting 'genes passing FDR<0.05' counts; although labelled as conditional, this reintroduces exactly the pseudo-inferential output the reference rules out and invites misreading. QC is thin by necessity (no PCA or sample-distance structure is possible with two samples) but the plan does report library sizes/size factors, an MA plot and a treated-vs-control scatter, plus duplicate-symbol and label checks; there is no outlier policy. The filter (≥10 counts in at least one sample, with retained/dropped reported) and in-model normalization (median-of-ratios or TMM, size factors reported, pseudocount stated) are appropriate; the contrast direction and label-reading from metadata are explicit though no design formula exists to specify. Enrichment is arguably unwarranted on an unreplicated ranking and its ORA/GSEA p-values risk lending false weight, though it is well-scoped (filtered universe reported, human WikiPathways named, leading-edge counts, mapping rate) apart from missing collection version and gene-set size window.
